lead: L134 -- the exotic sector of the 27 (27 = 16 + 10 + 1)
title: Prior-art scout: the E6 exotics, what makes them heavy, and whether that is an input
lane: scouting only; no verdict on the object; Gate 5 untouched; nothing promotes to CLAIMS.md

headline.a_is_it_a_discovery: NO -- REPRODUCTION. The literature half of L134 is already banked twice, in B951 (PRIOR_ART_HYPERCHARGE.md, section 'The exotics in 10 + 1, and the requirement that they be heavy') and B962 (PRIOR_ART_VEV.md, section Q5c). The record's repeated phrase 'the record has never addressed them' is FALSE AS WRITTEN. What is genuinely absent is any COMPUTATION.
headline.b_what_is_required: One mechanism everywhere: W contains kappa * S * D * Dbar, so M_D = kappa * <S>, and <S> is the U(1)'-breaking VEV. Plus an ad hoc discrete symmetry (Z2^L or Z2^B) to remove either the leptoquark or the diquark couplings, because both are present and their simultaneous presence gives rapid proton decay.
headline.c_input_or_derived: INPUT -- and sharper: NOT AN ADDITIONAL INPUT. It is the SAME input as the 27 VEV, consumed at the SAME step. The unique direction in the 27 that gives the exotics mass is S = omega_1 = the rank-1 element of J3(O) whose E6 stabiliser is Spin(10) -- exactly B962's first forced 27 VEV. Therefore L134 is a COROLLARY of the rank-reduction question (L133), not a second independent gap, and it is STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL TO THE VEV SITUATION -- not a defect peculiar to this object.
headline.d_no_go: No absolute no-go found. One sharp CONDITIONAL no-go (the trilemma) and one STRUCTURAL bound (derived here) exist; see 'no_go_findings'.

arithmetic_correction.the_error: GUT_REQUIREMENTS_LEDGER.md states verbatim '10 + 1 = 12 states per generation are EXOTIC'. 10 + 1 = 11.
arithmetic_correction.resolution: Both numbers are right, of different things. TWELVE counts against a 15-fermion SM generation and therefore INCLUDES nu_R. The repo says BOTH 'the 16 is one SM generation with a right-handed neutrino' AND 'the 10 + 1 are twelve' -- those cannot both hold.
arithmetic_correction.recommended_wording: eleven exotic states beyond the 16 (twelve beyond a 15-fermion generation, counting nu_R)
arithmetic_correction.certified: the arithmetic is certain (computed); whether 'twelve' is standard literature phrasing was NOT confirmed -- web-search budget exhausted

computation_done_here.built_from: the E6 Cartan matrix only; the 27 as the Weyl orbit of omega_1 (minuscule, so exact and complete -- asserted: 27 weights, all Dynkin labels in {-1,0,1})
computation_done_here.why_the_gradings_are_forced: a U(1) annihilating the so(10) simple roots is affine in n_1 alone; one annihilating the su(5) simple roots is affine in (n_1, n_2) alone; hypercharge lies in the su(5) Cartan so it carries no constant term. These are derivations, not ansaetze.
fits_are_predictive: psi fitted on the 1 and the 16 -> PREDICTED psi(10) = -2 (standard value -2)
chi fitted on the 16's three pieces + the singlet -> PREDICTED the 10's two pieces at +2, -2 (standard values)
Y fitted on the 16 ONLY -> PREDICTED Y(S) = 0, Y(nu^c) = 0, and the whole exotic 10 as (3,1)_-1/3 + (3,1)_+1/3 + (1,2)_+1/2 + (1,2)_-1/2

results.R1_no_bare_mass_inside_one_27: zero bilinears have (psi,chi) = (0,0). MB12: the test CAN pass (a self-conjugate rep such as the 26 of F4 contains charge-conjugate pairs) and CAN fail. It is a real test, and it fails.
results.R4_significance: S = omega_1 = the rank-1 element of J3(O), E6 stabiliser Spin(10) -- exactly B962's first forced 27 VEV
results.R5_theorem_rep_independent: the exotic pair carries psi = -4 as a fact about the E6 WEIGHT LATTICE, so ANY field in ANY E6 representation whose VEV gives it mass carries psi = +4 != 0. EXOTIC MASS != 0 ==> U(1)_psi BROKEN. No evasion by enlarging the Higgs sector.

R6_cubic_monomials_present_in_the_E6_inv.method: Sym^3(27) contains the E6 singlet once, so x_a x_b x_c occurs iff the three weights sum to zero

R6_cubic_monomials_present_in_the_E6_inv.significance: the Higgs doublets and the exotic triplets sit in the SAME two multiplets, so the leptoquark and diquark operators are components of the very invariants that give the quarks their masses. This is WHY Langacker's constraint is structural rather than accidental.
R6_cubic_monomials_present_in_the_E6_inv.caveat: the SU(5) tensor structures 10x10 contains 5bar and 10x5bar contains 5 are standard SU(5) algebra -- CITED, NOT RE-DERIVED; the E6 charge selection and the monomial census ARE derived here

computation_done_here.scope: everything is scoped to the GUT chain E6 > SO(10) x U(1)_psi > SU(5) x U(1)_chi x U(1)_psi; 'the exotics' means the 10 + 1 of THAT SO(10). It says nothing about the object's own cascade, whose u(1)^3 is a different rank-3 torus.

b_what_e6_model_building_requires.mass_mechanism: W contains kappa_ijk S_i D_j Dbar_k; M_D = kappa <S>
b_what_e6_model_building_requires.the_scale_is_not_free: <S> is the U(1)'-breaking VEV, so M_D / M_Z' = kappa / (g' Q_S) up to O(1) -- a RATIO OF COUPLINGS, not of scales. Perturbativity on kappa caps how far the exotics can be pushed above the Z'.

constraints.detail: both leptoquark and diquark operators are present (computed, R6). Simultaneous presence gives rapid proton decay. Fix used everywhere: an AD HOC discrete symmetry -- Z2^L (exotics become diquarks) or Z2^B (leptoquarks), never both. Nevzorov proposes a single Z~2^H.

the D, D^c couplings are related BY E6 to the ordinary Higgs Yukawas and give rapid proton decay unless their masses (and therefore the U(1)' breaking scale) are comparable to the unification scale; a TeV-scale Z' therefore requires that the GUT Yukawa relations are NOT respected
constraints.status: CITED, NOT RE-DERIVED (Langacker RMP 81 (2009) 1199, banked in B951)

constraints.detail: Kang-Langacker-Nelson quote m_D > 250 GeV (Tevatron leptoquark) and > 190 GeV (quasi-stable). STALE, 2008 vintage. Modern LHC vector-like-quark pair-production bounds sit near 1.3-1.5 TeV. NOT re-derived here.
if quasi-stable (decay only via dim-5 operators), full BBN constraints in the (tau, Y_X) plane across the 1e-2 to 1e12 s windows (Kang-Langacker-Nelson section III.3)

constraints.c: the obligation does not end at 'heavy'
constraints.detail: the LIGHTEST exotic quark must also be made UNSTABLE, which in E6-inspired models requires EXTRA TeV-scale vector-like lepton or down-type quark states (Nevzorov 1205.5967, abstract)

'the anomalies are cancelled automatically if the low-energy spectrum involves complete representations of E6' (King-Moretti-Nevzorov). Projecting the exotics out COSTS automatic anomaly freedom, and the anomaly check becomes non-vacuous exactly when the spectrum is incomplete. This is L132's amended gate arrived at from the other side.

c_input_or_derived.plainly: M_D = kappa <S> has two free parameters and NOTHING derives either. No source found this sweep derives the exotic mass scale from anything.
c_input_or_derived.the_stronger_and_more_useful_statement: It is not an ADDITIONAL input on top of the 27 VEV -- it is the SAME input at the SAME step. The unique mass-giving direction is S = omega_1, the rank-1 element whose stabiliser is Spin(10); <S> != 0 IS the step E6 -> SO(10), rank 6 -> 5.
consequences_for_the_programme: L134 is STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL to the VEV situation (B962: the VEV direction is always an input; nobody's object supplies one). It is NOT a defect peculiar to this object and should not be written up as one.
L134 should be MERGED into the VEV/rank row of the ledger, not carried as an independent open item. Carrying it separately double-counts one gap.

What L134 adds that the VEV row does not: the SELECTION RULE (which direction, uniquely) IS derived, and it lands on the same rank-1 orbit the programme already computed. That is a consistency check the programme PASSES, not a new failure.

the_one_partial_derivation_route.claim: in string constructions the massless spectrum is fixed by topology (bundle cohomology / Wilson-line or hypercharge-flux projection), so exotics can be PROJECTED OUT rather than made heavy, at the price of incomplete multiplets
the_one_partial_derivation_route.evidence: Palti 1601.00285 -- and note it reproduces the same structure independently: 'The exotics are not vector-like under the U(1) symmetry and therefore their mass is naturally related to its breaking scale'
the_one_partial_derivation_route.status: NOT CERTIFIED. This sweep did NOT read a primary source on the Wilson-line projection of E6 exotics. Even in this route the compactification is the input.

no_go_findings.absolute_no_go: NONE FOUND. Nothing says 'there exists an E6 model that cannot make its exotics heavy' as a theorem.

D1_the_trilemma.statement: {E6-related Yukawa relations} + {TeV-scale U(1)' breaking} + {proton stability} are MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT. Any two hold; the third must be given up -- in practice by imposing a discrete symmetry that breaks the E6 relations.
D1_the_trilemma.status: CITED, NOT RE-DERIVED; banked in B951

D2_the_structural_bound.statement: exotic mass != 0 ==> U(1)_psi broken. M_D/M_Z' is a COUPLING ratio, not a scale ratio, so the exotics cannot be decoupled while leaving the extra U(1) light.

D3_independent_framework_corroboration.statement: F-theory SU(5)xU(1) with hypercharge flux: exotics 'are not vector-like under the U(1) symmetry and therefore their mass is naturally related to its breaking scale'; the spectrum 'does not form complete GUT representations'; 'the exotics cannot form a complete 10 multiplet'

D4_the_obligation_does_not_end_at_heavy.statement: the lightest exotic quark must also be made unstable, requiring extra TeV vector-like matter

D5_string_side.statement: string consistency conditions FORCE quasi-chiral exotics in many constructions, and 'mass generation for the fermions is sometimes problematic'. Not a theorem.
